senses.gloss: Paulastya^1 (“son of Pulastya”) = Kubera: II, 417; III, †12364 (Dhanadaṃ); V, 7543.

Paulastya^4, pl. (ºāḥ) (“sons or descendants of Pulastya”). § 130 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2724, 2726 (i.e. Rākshasas, reborn as the sons of Dhṛtarāshṭra).--§ 532 (Sītāsāntvana): III, 280, 16154 (ºkulaghātinaḥ, sc. Rāvaṇa).--§ 535 (Setubandhana): III, 283, 16304 (ºpāṃsanaṃ, sc. Rāvaṇa).-§ 600 (Ghaṭotkacavadhap.): VII, 156, 6842 (ºair Yātudhānaiś ca, a class of Rākshasas).
Paulastya^5, adj. (“belonging to Pulastya”?). § 59 (Saṃśaptakavadhap.): VII, 23, 1040 (dhanuḥ, held by Ghaṭotkaca).

Pauloma^1, adj. (“relating to Pulomā or Puloman,” sc. parvan) = Paulomaparvan. § 4 (Anukram.): I, 1, 88 (ºāstīkamūlavān, sc. Bhāratadrumaḥ).--§ 10 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 304, 312.--§ 11 (do.): I, 2, 360, 365.
Pauloma^2, a tīrtha. § 250 (Arjunavanavāsap.): I, 216, 7841 (tīrthaṃ, one of the five Nārītīrthāni).

Pauloma^3, pl. (ºāḥ), a tribe of Asuras. § 11 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 460 (ºaiḥ Kālakeyaiś ca yatra yuddhaṃ Kirīṭinaḥ, cf. § 445).--§ 445 (Nivātakavacayuddhap.): III, 173, 12198 (ºaiḥ Kālakañjaiś ca, in Hiraṇyapura), 12208 (the offspring of Pulomā, in Hiraṇyapura), 12209 (mahāsuraiḥ, destroyed by Arjuna).--§ 552 (Goharaṇap.): IV, 45, 1431 (defeated by Arjuna, all. to § 445).--§ 552d (Arjuna): IV, 61, 1976 (ºān Kālakañjāṃś ca, vanquished by Arjuna, all. to § 445). --§ 561d (Nara-Nārāyaṇau): V, 49, 1930 (do., slain by Nara (i.e. Arjuna), all. to § 445).--§ 593 (Abhimanyuvadhap.): VII, 51, 1998 (Hiraṇyapuravāsinaḥ…Pºāḥ sagaṇā hatāḥ, sc. by Arjuna, all. to § 445). Cf. next.

[Paulomaparvan], the fourth of the minor parvans. (Cf. Pauloma^1.) § 18: Sauti's conversation, in the forest of Naimisha, with the ṛshis at the twelve years' sacrifice of Śaunaka (I, 4).--§ 19: Śaunaka's lineage from Brahmán through Bhṛgu, Cyavana, Prcmati, Ruru, and Śunaka was related to him by Sauti.--§ 20: Pulomā.--§§ 21--3: Pramadvarā.--§§ 24--5: From this time Ruru made a vow to destroy the serpents, and whenever he saw a serpent he always killed it. Sahasrapad (q.v.) directed Ruru to ascertain the facts about the serpent-sacrifice of Janamejaya and the deliverance of the serpents by Āstīka; Ruru, having come home, asked his father, who related all about the story (I, 9--12)
